approved: Sugar Research and Development Services (Consequential Amendments—Excise) Bill 2013

Supported the Sugar Research and Development Services bills as a reform backed by most of the industry, under which Sugar Research Australia would replace separate research bodies and receive a 70c per tonne levy paid equally by growers and mills, while raising concerns about consultation, regional research, conflicts of interest and the legislation's rushed 1 July 2013 commencement.

Supported the Sugar Research and Development Services bills, saying they would consolidate research functions in Sugar Research Australia, reduce duplication and secure funding through a 70c per tonne levy, while urging swift passage to provide certainty for research staff and the industry's future.
Sugar Research and Development Services (Consequential Amendments—Excise) Act 2013
